newsitem.title: USA: Monsanto seen buying Iowa seed company - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Monsanto seen buying Iowa seed company - analysts.

text.p: Monsanto Co is expected to purchase an Iowa-based seed company, enabling it to expand its agricultural operations, analysts said.
Dain Bosworth analyst Bonnie Wittenburg said she expects Monsanto to buy Holden Foundation Seeds, paying as much as $900 million.
"According to various sources in the seed industry, Holden Foundation Seeds is expected to announce soon that it is being sold to Monsanto Co," Wittenburg said in a report.
A Monsanto spokeswoman declined to comment on the speculation.
A Holden executive did not return a call requesting comment.
Holden, which is privately held, said in December that it would be sold after the first of the year, said Piper Jaffray analyst George Dahlman.
He said Monsanto is expected to purchase Holden, with prices for the seed company rumored to be $600 million to as much as $1.0 billion.
Holden sells germplasm -- or plant breeding stock --- to small seed companies. Analysts said Holden's germplasm will give Monsanto an outlet for its biotechnology developments.
Monsanto and other agricultural companies have developed new crops that are genetically enhanced to have special traits, including resistance to certain insects.

Monsanto also has developed crops, including soybeans, that are resistant to use of its Roundup herbicide. That enables farmers to spray Roundup on their fields to kill weeds without harming the crop.

"We believe a significant portion of Monsanto's motivation to bid for Holden is to get access to germplasm that can serve as a delivery vehicle for Monsanto's Roundup herbicide and biotech technologies...," Wittenburg said.
She added that the deal also would be a "defensive play to keep anyone else from obtaining Holden."
"Monsanto needs to gain commercial outlets for its technology and it needs to lock out competitive technologies," Dahlman said.

Monsanto is focusing on its agricultural operations that are the centerpiece of its life sciences business. The company, which recently announced plans to spin off its chemical business, also has food ingredient and pharmaceutical units.
